rbin 0.3.0

CRAN release: 2026-11-19

This release combines the unreleased 0.2.2 and 0.2.3 fixes and both fresh audits. Results change from CRAN 0.2.1 for missing-value placement, winsorized assignment, dropped missing responses, tie-aware frequency groups and factor counts.

Shared binning and response handling

  • Character responses are sorted in byte (C-locale) order: uppercase before lowercase, ASCII before accented characters; use a factor to choose the event level. The second value is the event on every machine (fx6 opus M1).
  • All numeric binning functions and rbin_create() accept bare column names, strings and variables holding names, including long non-syntactic names, consistently with rbin_factor() (rx2h-L2 / rx2d-L1).
  • Empty intervals retain zero counts, undefined rates/WoE and zero IV/entropy; summaries join by bin ID and retain a separate final missing group (H01).
  • Pure groups have entropy zero, including printed totals (H06).
  • Responses must be 0/1, logical, or binary factor/character; factors use their first level as 0 and second as 1. Invalid responses error; missing responses are dropped with a warning. All methods accept data.table input (H12, H13, H14).
  • Declared binary factor responses keep their coding when only one class is observed. Explicit NA response levels are treated as missing, while extra unused levels remain supported when two classes are observed (A2-M04, Hydrogen M3).
  • Final numeric intervals have no upper bound, including when adding one to a large finite maximum has no effect (H11).
  • Bin counts must be whole numbers; interval methods require at least two bins, and equal-frequency binning permits one bin (M03).

Numeric binning and dummy variables

  • rbin_equal_length() and rbin_winsorize() compute cut points only from values with absolute value up to 1e300 (for rbin_winsorize(), the values after winsorizing) and otherwise stop with a message, because near the double-precision limit exact-cut membership would depend on the platform. rbin_create() still scores any finite value into the first or last bin.

  • Predictor classes: I() (AsIs) columns are binned as their numbers; integer64 and difftime predictors are refused by the numeric methods and rbin_create() with a message on how to convert them (difftime units can differ between fitting and scoring data); factor, Date and POSIXct predictors point to rbin_factor() / rbin_factor_create(). rbin_factor() accepts classed predictors except integer64.

  • rbin_create() rejects incompatible bins objects with a class diagnostic, while valid all-missing fits still produce no indicators (fx6 astra M7).

  • Winsorized binning validates winsor_rate as a single number in [0, 0.5], including when clamp endpoints are supplied. remove_na = FALSE gives a clear error for retained missing predictors (fx6 opus M2 / astra M8).

  • Fitters and rbin_create() reject integer64 and other unsupported numeric classes before arithmetic, with conversion guidance for integer64 values within +/-2^53 (fx6 H2).

  • Equal-width and winsorized cuts multiply the span before division, keeping observations on exact mathematical boundaries in the left-closed bin. Large integer spans no longer emit integer overflow warnings (fx6 H1, M6).

  • Quantile binning rejects computed NA/NaN cut points, including interpolation between negative and positive infinity, while valid infinite cuts remain supported. Numeric assignment rejects unmatched non-missing values rather than putting them into a missing bin (rx2h-H1).

  • Equal-frequency dummy names format all boundaries together, preserving the precision of the final >= threshold (rx2h-L1).

  • Manual display bounds stay ordered when cuts lie outside the observed predictor range (rx2h-L3).

  • rbin_equal_length() handles empty intervals and computes finite internal edges even when the finite range overflows; equal-width and winsorized methods reject infinite predictors (H01, A2-H05).

  • rbin_quantiles() constructs probabilities directly as integer fractions, preserving exact cut-point membership and derived statistics (A2-H06).

  • rbin_winsorize() treats supplied endpoints as clamp values, estimates only unspecified endpoints, rejects reversed limits, and handles missing predictors with include_na = FALSE (H04).

  • rbin_equal_freq() now keeps tied values together using empirical quantiles, returning fewer non-empty bins with a message when cuts coincide. Counts can differ from 0.2.1, and rbin_create() dummies match the non-missing training summary. Untied sizes differ by at most one; more bins than observations still error and missing predictors retain a separate final group (H02, A2-H01).

  • rbin_create() preserves bin order, keeps columns for absent bins, makes colliding boundary labels distinct, and assigns values outside the training range to the outer intervals (H03, H10).

  • rbin_create() uses equal-frequency dummy names describing the actual scoring thresholds, including gaps (A2-L01).

  • rbin_create() applies stored winsor clamp endpoints before scoring, including collapsed fitted ranges and limits outside the training range. Older saved winsorized objects without clamp metadata must be fitted again (A2-H02).

  • Numeric WoE plots include the missing-predictor group (H15).

Factor binning and dummy variables

  • Genuine missing values also display as (missing) when an explicit NA factor level is present, in both printed summaries and plot ticks (rx3-L1).
  • Printed factor summaries and plot ticks label genuine missing values as (missing) when a literal "NA" category is also present, preserving the usual display and stored typed labels otherwise (rx2d-L2).
  • rbin_factor() groups on integer IDs, preserving distinct numeric and temporal categories whose display text collides, and preserving explicit NA factor levels separately from missing codes. NaN and NA numeric predictors share one missing bin; all retained observations contribute to counts and statistics (A2-H03, A2-H04, Hydrogen H1, Hydrogen H2, Hydrogen H3).
  • rbin_factor() preserves ordered classes and explicit NA level metadata; include_na = FALSE removes missing codes while retaining explicit NA levels (Hydrogen M4, Hydrogen M5).
  • rbin_factor() accepts bare, character and indirect column names, including long non-syntactic names, and labels missing plot ticks as NA (Hydrogen M2, Hydrogen M6).
  • rbin_factor_combine() matches exact names without regex or substring effects and preserves ordered factors, explicit NA levels and unselected missing codes. Selecting NA consistently combines both kinds of NA with the new level (H05, A2-M01, Hydrogen H4, Hydrogen H5, Hydrogen M5).
  • rbin_factor_create() preserves original columns, accepts character predictors, creates indicators from factor codes (including explicit NA levels), and makes generated names unique. Zero-level inputs return unchanged (H07, H08, H09, A2-M02, Hydrogen M1).

Addins

  • Factor addin options use distinct IDs for literal "NA" and explicit NA levels; selecting the NA level combines the intended rows (fx6 H3).
  • Both addins use the shared binning workers, drop missing responses with a warning, and accept data.table input (H13, H14).
  • Both addins accept their default NULL argument and supplied data.frame expressions (H16).
  • An explicitly changed, unresolved Data Name now validates instead of silently using the originally supplied frame (A2-M03).

Documentation and metadata

  • Maintainer email updated to aravindhebbali@rsquaredacademy.com (M01).
  • Declare data.table >= 1.9.4 and testthat >= 3.1.7, the first version providing the mocking API used by the regression tests (M02, A2-M05).
  • Submission comments describe only checks actually run (M04).
  • Document all 17 mbank columns, correct S3 return structures/classes and the book DOI 10.1002/9781119201731 (M05, L01, L02).
  • Regenerate README, vignette and website output, including reference examples, data documentation and NEWS (A2-M06).
  • Manual cut-point documentation now distinguishes the integer +1 recipe from continuous open upper bounds (A2-L02).
  • Factor documentation describes column-name arguments, supported predictor classes, group order and missing-value policies (Hydrogen L1, Hydrogen L2).
  • Attaching the package no longer contacts CRAN for updates.
